segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Good afternoon everybody and welcome to Riverside Industrial Village.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: To start your visit I' m just going to give you a brief account of the history of the museum before letting you roam about on your own.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I won't keep you long.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: OK?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now, from where we're standing you've got a good view of the river over there.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And it was because of this fast-flowing water that this site was a natural place for manufacturing works.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The water and the availability of raw materials in the area, like minerals and iron ore, and also the abundance of local fuels, like coal and firewood, all made this site suitable for industry from a very early time.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Water was the main source of power for the early industries and some of the water wheels were first established in the twelfth century, would you believe?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: At that time, local craftsmen first built an iron forge just behind the village here, on the bend in the river.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: By the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the region's rivers supported more than a hundred and ~ water mills - and many of these continued to operate well into the nineteenth century.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But then the steam engine was invented and then the railways came and the centres of industry were able to move away from the rivers and the countryside and into the towns.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So, industrial villages like this one became very rare.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So that's the history for you.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you'd like any more information, you can ask me some questions, or you can read further in our excellent guide book.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now I'm going to give you a plan of the site and I'd just like to point out where everything is and then you can take a look at everything for yourself.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I've already pointed out the river, which is on the left.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And of course, running along the bottom is Woodside Road, got it?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now we're standing at the entrance, see it at the bottom. and immediately to our right is the Ticket Office.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You won't need that because you've got your group booking, but just past it are the toilets- ·always good to know where they are.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In front of us is the car park, as you can see, and to the left, by the entry gate is the Gift Shop.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: That's where you can get copies of the guide, like this one here.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now, beyond the car park all the buildings are arranged in a half circle with a yard in the middle.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The big, stone building at the top is the main Workshop.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: That's where the furnace is and where all the metal was smelted and the tools were cast, as you'll be able to see.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now, in the top right-hand corner. that building with bigger windows is the Showroom, where samples of all the tools that were made through the ages are on display.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In the top left corner is the Grinding Shop, where the tools were sharpened and finished.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And on one side of that you can see the Engine Room and on the other is the .G.afu. which isn't an antique, you'll be pleased to know, though they do serve very nice old-fashioned teas.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The row of buildings you can see on the left are the cottages.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: These were built for the workers towards the end of the eighteenth century and they're still furnished from that period so you can get a good idea of ordinary people's living conditions.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Across the yard from them, you can see the stables where the horses were kept for transporting the products.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And the separate building in front of them is the Works Office and that still has some of the old accounts on display.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Right, if anyone wants a guided tour then I'm starting at the Engine Room.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you'd like to come along. this way please. ladies and gentlemen.
